newsitem.title: USA: 40 percent of U.S. households own a PC, report says.
newsitem.headline: 40 percent of U.S. households own a PC, report says.

text.p: About 41 million U.S. households, or 40 percent of the total, own at least one personal computer, but the rate at which additional households are buying PCs seems to be slowing, research firm Computer Intelligence said Monday.

The firm's poll of 17,500 households found that higher-income and better-educated households were more likely to own a PC. About 60 percent of households with more than $40,000 in income have at least one PC, compared with 24 percent in households that have income less than $35,000.
In addition, 52 percent of households with children have a PC.
But PC penetration into the home seems to be slowing. Overall penetration rose only 2.2 percentage points in 1996, or about half the rate seen in the previous two years, Computer Intelligence said.

In the past week, technology stocks have slumped amid warnings from some PC component makers that the second quarter will be a weak one. Intel Corp., the world's largest computer chip maker, also warned two weeks ago that it expects European sales to be weak.
The warnings have raised concerns that the PC market could grow less than expected this year, analysts said.
Computer Intelligence conducted the survey by mail.
